subject: POC traffic handoff + staging plan and validation checklist
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlasai.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + immediate asks for POC traffic handoff

Hi Samir / Lina —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick off the staging validation next week: 

Summary from our side:
- POC goal: validate 1) throughput at peak bursts (RPS up to 450), 2) per-request latency SLO under burst (p95 < 450ms), and 3) end-to-end quality on your summarization prompts.
- Workload profile: mixed chat + summarization. Typical token lengths: 40–120 tokens for chat, 400–1,200 tokens for summarization. Median token length ~210.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrency target 60 concurrent sessions; bursts to 450 RPS for 2–5 minute windows.

Immediate asks (action owners in parentheses):
1) Send a 24-hour representative traffic sample (CSV with timestamp,rps,avg_tokens_per_request) and 3–5 example prompts for the summarization task (Samir) — needed by 2028-06-14 EOD.
2) Confirm staging environment access (VPC peering or temporary SSH tunnel) + contact for infra (Lina) — by 2028-06-13.
3) We will provision a burst-capacity reservation and a mirrored staging stack; Ben will own the test harness and token-trace instrumentation.
4) Proposed POC timeline: onboarding & staging validation (1 week), load tests and tuning (1 week), acceptance window + quality evals (1 week). Total ~3 weeks from staging sign-off.

Attachments: poc-eval-deck-v2.pdf (POC plan + success criteria), atlas-traffic-sample.csv (example schema). Drive link with prompts and eval rubric attached here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XAtlAs-POC-deck

Next call: propose 2028-06-15 10:00am PT for a 30-min staging handshake (we'll send calendar invite once access confirmed).

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Samir Patel <samir@atlasai.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-12T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + immediate asks for POC traffic handoff

Thanks Neha — this is very clear. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 450 RPS burst comes from our edge orchestrator; it's not sustained per user but from parallel webhook fanout. Bursts typically last 2–4 minutes, sometimes up to 6 in peak shopping events (we've added a sample spike trace).
- Token lengths for summarization can hit 1,400 tokens in ~1% of requests. We've truncated in the CSV to 1200 for brevity but can provide raw lengths.
- Staging access: we prefer a temporary API key + allowlist of Redwood's staging IPs. Lina will coordinate (cc'd).

Attached: atlas-traffic-sample.csv (24h sample) and a short CSV with the 5 representative prompts. Also attaching our internal SLOs doc — note that we have a stricter p99 target internally but happy to run p95-first for the POC.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering | AtlasAI
samir@atlasai.com
+1 (646) 555-0123

Attachments: atlas-traffic-sample.csv (csv), atlas-prompts-sample.csv (csv)

Neha / Samir —

Thanks for the sample. I pulled the CSV and spot-checked timestamps — good distribution. Quick notes on what I'll prepare before the staging handshake: 
- Test harness: continuous-load runner with ability to emulate your burst shape (we'll parameterize the 2–6 minute windows).
- Instrumentation: token-level tracing (per-request tokens_in/tokens_out), backend latency buckets, and an optional KV-cache probe to measure prefix cache hit rates.
- Staging infra: we'll request allowlist for our staging IP ranges; if you prefer API-key gating we can generate scoped keys with expiring TTL.

Can you confirm whether the 1% requests with 1,400 tokens need to be included in the first acceptance run? If yes, we should reserve a slightly larger VM type for the initial burst capacity.

I'll draft the staging runbook and attach a preflight checklist (env vars, synthetic vs. recorded replay toggles) ahead of the handshake.

- Ben

Samir — thanks for the uploads, got them. Quick answers: 
- Include the 1% 1,400-token cases in the acceptance run (we'll mark them as rare but critical). Ben — please size initial burst reservation to account for that tail.
- Lina, can you confirm allowlist method? If API-key + allowlist is easiest, we can issue scoped keys that expire after 2 weeks.

Proposed revised timeline: 
- 2028-06-14: staging access confirmed, Ben shares runbook + preflight checklist.
- 2028-06-15: 30-min handshake call at 10:00am PT to walk the runbook and finalize peak window shapes.
- 2028-06-17–21: load tests and tuning.
- 2028-06-24–26: acceptance window & quality evals.

I've updated the eval deck in Drive with your traffic notes. I'll send the calendar invite for 6/15 once Lina confirms access method.

Neha
